summary: The Tomb of Returning Names becomes an authored dungeon record of the design bible's twelve spaces, the four authored tomb cells carry a dungeonContext block naming their space and site rules, and Rust selects the elven or the corrupted rule set from S9's DungeonContext owner.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at 2ec3243. The four tomb world cells are touched in exactly one added line each (the dungeonContext block, inserted before admission), so other lanes editing those files merge cleanly. tools/src/validate.mjs takes one new block plus one line in the world-cell block; tools/src/build-content-bundle.mjs takes dungeons in the domain list. godot-rust/src/strategy/dungeon.rs is NOT edited: S9 owns it, and the authored-record reader is a different responsibility from the context and its signature, so it lives in a new strategy/dungeon_content.rs that imports DungeonContext rather than restating anything in it. That is move 1 (build on it), not a second dungeon module: nothing in dungeon.rs is copied or shadowed. Duplication that does exist is deliberate and held equal: a cell's dungeonContext.siteRuleIds mirrors its space's default-owner list in the dungeon record, and both validate.mjs and the Rust reader refuse a mismatch, so the record is the owner and the cell is the mirror.

The reader lives in a new strategy/dungeon_content.rs because reading an authored record is a different responsibility from folding a context into a signature, and dungeon.rs is S9's file at 1,103 lines; the new module imports DungeonContext and ConceptKey and restates nothing. strategy/mod.rs takes one declaration beside dungeon's: passed

Six of the twelve bible spaces have a world cell, not four as the card assumed: world.cell.reception_terrace and world.cell.processional_ramp realise spaces 1 and 2 and were authored before this card. They are outside this lane's owned file set and carry no dungeonContext block; the record names them and says so. Only B6's four tomb_* interior cells carry the block: not_run

Space-to-cell mapping is authored from each cell's own evidence and every mapping carries its reasoning in the record's note: tomb_threshold -> registry_court (the sealed name registers and the site's first evidence inspect), tomb_reception -> petition_gallery (the speaking stone answers a petitioner; the service opening is the retreat exit), tomb_service_passage -> service_crawl (the cramped bypass and its grave-goods cache), tomb_archive_core -> flooded_archive (the ledger, the site's textual evidence). No thirteenth space was invented and none of the bible's twelve was dropped: not_run

Site rules are opaque IDs and nothing reads a rule's meaning. A7 owns what a site rule does and no rule registry exists; site_rule.tomb.grave_watch is A7's card's own ID, carried verbatim. No suppressed_site_rules, no Battle::new change, no CellDefinition field -- all A7's: not_run
